questions.q: Who among the following constitute the National Development Council? 1️⃣ The Prime Minister 2️⃣ The Chairman, Finance Commission 3️⃣ Ministers of the Union Cabinet 4️⃣ Chief Ministers of the States
questions.e: The National Development Council (NDC) comprises the Prime Minister, all Union Cabinet Ministers, Chief Ministers of all States/Union Territories, and members of the Planning Commission (now NITI Aayog). The Chairman of the Finance Commission is not a member of the NDC.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: The Parliamentary Committee on Public Accounts 1️⃣ consists of not more than 25 Members of the Lok Sabha 2️⃣ scrutinizes appropriation and finance accounts of the Government 3️⃣ examines the report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
questions.e: The Public Accounts Committee consists of 22 members (15 from Lok Sabha and 7 from Rajya Sabha). Its primary functions include scrutinizing the appropriation and finance accounts of the Government of India and examining the audit reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG).

questions.q: In the context of India, which of the following principles is/are implied institutionally in the parliamentary government? 1️⃣ Members of the Cabinet are Members of the Parliament. 2️⃣ Ministers hold the office till they enjoy confidence in the Parliament. 3️⃣ Cabinet is headed by the Head of the State.
questions.e: In a parliamentary system, ministers must be members of the legislature, and the executive is responsible to the legislature, holding office only as long as they enjoy its confidence. The Cabinet is headed by the Prime Minister (Head of Government), not the Head of State (President).

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Council of Ministers in the Centre shall be collectively responsible to the Parliament. 2️⃣ The Union Ministers shall hold the office during the pleasure of the President of India. 3️⃣ The Prime Minister shall communicate to the President about the proposals for legislation.
questions.e: Under Article 75, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible specifically to the Lok Sabha, not the entire Parliament. Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President, and the Prime Minister is constitutionally obligated to communicate legislative proposals to the President.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ National Development Council is an organ of the Planning Commission. 2️⃣ The Economic and Social Planning is kept in the Concurrent List in the Constitution of India. 3️⃣ The Constitution of India prescribes that Panchayats should be assigned the task of preparation of plans for economic development and social justice.
questions.e: The NDC is an advisory body to the Planning Commission, not its organ. Economic and social planning is found in the Concurrent List. The 73rd Amendment mandates that Panchayats prepare plans for economic development and social justice.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Chairman and the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha are not the members of that House. 2️⃣ While the nominated members of the two Houses of the Parliament have no voting right in the presidential election, they have the right to vote in the election of the Vice President.
questions.e: The Chairman (Vice President) is not a member of Rajya Sabha, but the Deputy Chairman is a member of the House. Nominated members cannot vote for the President but do participate in the election of the Vice President.

questions.q: With reference to National Legal Services Authority, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Its objective is to provide free and competent legal services to the weaker sections of the society on the basis of equal opportunity. 2️⃣ It issues guidelines for the State Legal Services Authorities to implement the legal programmes and schemes throughout the country.
questions.e: NALSA was constituted to provide free legal aid to eligible weaker sections and to organize Lok Adalats. It is responsible for issuing guidelines and framing schemes for State Legal Services Authorities to follow.

questions.q: Under the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, who shall be the authority to initiate the process for determining the nature and extent of individual or community forest rights or both?
questions.e: As per the Forest Rights Act of 2006, the Gram Sabha is the primary authority designated to initiate the process of determining forest rights for individuals or communities.

questions.q: 'Economic Justice' as one of the objectives of the Indian Constitution has been provided in
o: the Preamble and the Fundamental Rights
the Preamble and the Directive Principles of State Policy
the Fundamental Rights and the Directive Principles of State Policy
questions.e: The Preamble lists 'Justice: social, economic and political' as an objective. The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) further mandate the state to secure a social order for the promotion of welfare, emphasizing economic justice.

questions.q: According to the Constitution of India, which of the following are fundamental for the governance of the country?
questions.e: Article 37 of the Constitution explicitly states that the Directive Principles of State Policy are fundamental in the governance of the country and it shall be the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.

questions.q: The sales tax you pay while purchasing a toothpaste is a
o: tax imposed and collected by the State Government
tax imposed by the State Government but collected by the Central Government
tax imposed by the Central Government but collected by the State Government
tax imposed by the Central Government
questions.e: At the time of this 2014 paper, sales tax (VAT) was a tax imposed and collected by the State Government under the Seventh Schedule. This has since been largely subsumed by GST.

questions.q: Which one of the following Schedules of the Constitution of India contains provisions regarding anti-defection?
questions.e: The Tenth Schedule, also known as the Anti-Defection Law, was added by the 52nd Amendment Act in 1985 to prevent political defections.

questions.q: In the Constitution of India, promotion of international peace and security is included in the
questions.e: Article 51 of the Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV) mandates the State to promote international peace and security and maintain just and honorable relations between nations.

questions.q: Which of the following are associated with 'Planning' in India? 1️⃣ The Finance Commission 2️⃣ The National Development Council 3️⃣ The Union Ministry of Rural Development 4️⃣ The Union Ministry of Urban Development 5️⃣ The Parliament
questions.e: The NDC reviews the national plan, and the Parliament provides the ultimate approval for planning objectives and allocations. The Finance Commission deals with fiscal transfers, not plan formulation.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are the function/functions of the Cabinet Secretariat? 1️⃣ Preparation of agenda for Cabinet Meetings 2️⃣ Secretarial assistance to Cabinet Committees 3️⃣ Allocation of financial resources to the Ministries
questions.e: The Cabinet Secretariat provides secretarial support to the Cabinet and its committees and prepares agendas. Financial allocation is the function of the Ministry of Finance.

questions.q: A Constitutional Government is one which 1️⃣ places effective restrictions on individual liberty in the interest of State Authority 2️⃣ places effective restrictions on the Authority of the State in the interest of individual liberty
questions.e: Constitutionalism implies "limited government." It protects individual liberty by placing legal and constitutional checks on the powers of the State.

questions.q: Which of the following are the discretionary powers given to the Governor of a State? 1️⃣ Sending a report to the President of India for imposing the President's rule 2️⃣ Appointing the Ministers 3️⃣ Reserving certain bills passed by the State Legislature for consideration of the President of India 4️⃣ Making the rules to conduct the business of the State Government
questions.e: Reporting for President's rule (Art 356) and reserving bills (Art 200) are constitutional discretionary powers. Appointing ministers and making business rules are usually done on the advice of the CM.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The President shall make rules for the more convenient transaction of the business of the Government of India, and for the allocation among Ministers of the said business. 2️⃣ All executive actions of the Government of India shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the Prime Minister.
questions.e: Article 77 states the President makes rules for government business. However, all executive actions are taken in the name of the President, not the Prime Minister.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding a No-Confidence Motion in India: 1️⃣ There is no mention of a No-Confidence Motion in the Constitution of India. 2️⃣ A Motion of No-Confidence can be introduced in the Lok Sabha only.
questions.e: The Constitution does not mention the motion; it is part of Rule 198 of the Lok Sabha Rules. Since the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, the motion can only be moved there.

questions.q: The power of the Supreme Court of India to decide disputes between the Centre and the States falls under its
questions.e: Under Article 131, the Supreme Court has exclusive original jurisdiction over disputes between the Union and one or more States.

questions.q: The power to increase the number of judges in the Supreme Court of India is vested in
questions.e: Article 124(1) empowers the Parliament to prescribe the number of judges in the Supreme Court.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Directive Principles of State Policy: 1️⃣ The Principles spell out the socio-economic democracy in the country. 2️⃣ The provisions contained in these Principles are not enforceable by any court.
questions.e: DPSPs aim to establish social and economic democracy. Article 37 explicitly states they are not enforceable by any court.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Rajya Sabha has no power either to reject or to amend a Money Bill. 2️⃣ The Rajya Sabha cannot vote on the Demands for Grants. 3️⃣ The Rajya Sabha cannot discuss the Annual Financial Statement.
questions.e: Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill within 14 days and cannot vote on demands for grants. However, it can and does discuss the Annual Financial Statement (Budget).

questions.q: The Government of India Act of 1919 clearly defined
o: the separation of power between the judiciary and the legislature
the jurisdiction of the central and provincial governments
the powers of the Secretary of State for India and the Viceroy
questions.e: The 1919 Act (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) relaxed central control by demarcating and separating central and provincial subjects.

questions.q: When a bill is referred to a joint sitting of both the Houses of the Parliament, it has to be passed by
o: three-fourths majority of members present and voting
a simple majority of members present and voting
questions.e: At a joint sitting (Art 108), the bill is passed by a simple majority of the total number of members of both Houses present and voting.

questions.q: The Government of India has established NITI Aayog to replace the
questions.e: NITI Aayog was formed via an executive resolution on January 1, 2015, replacing the 65-year-old Planning Commission.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Executive Power of the Union of India is vested in the Prime Minister. 2️⃣ The Prime Minister is the ex officio Chairman of the Civil Services Board.
questions.e: Executive power is vested in the President (Art 53). The Cabinet Secretary, not the PM, is the ex-officio Chairman of the Civil Services Board.

questions.q: The provisions in Fifth Schedule and Sixth Schedule in the Constitution of India are made in order to
o: protect the interests of all the border States
determine the powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats
protect the interests of Scheduled Tribes
questions.e: Both schedules provide for the administration of scheduled and tribal areas to safeguard the interests of Scheduled Tribes.

questions.q: With reference to the Union Government, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Department of Revenue is responsible for the preparation of Union Budget that is presented to the Parliament. 2️⃣ No amount can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India without the authorization from the Parliament of India. 3️⃣ All the disbursements made from Public Account also need the authorization from the Parliament of India.
questions.e: The Department of Economic Affairs, not Revenue, prepares the budget. Appropriation from the Consolidated Fund requires Parliamentary law (Art 114). Public Account payments do not require such authorization.

questions.q: Who/Which of the following is the custodian of the Constitution of India?
questions.e: The Supreme Court acts as the final interpreter and guardian of the Constitution through its power of judicial review.

questions.q: Which one of the following was given classical language status recently?
questions.e: Odia was declared a classical language in 2014, making it the 6th language to receive the status.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Legislative Council of a State in India can be larger in size than half of the Legislative Assembly of that particular State. 2️⃣ The Governor of State nominates the Chairman of Legislative Council of that particular State.
questions.e: The maximum strength of the Council is fixed at one-third of the Assembly (Art 171). The Chairman is elected by the Council members from among themselves.

questions.q: "To uphold and protect the Sovereignty, Unity and Integrity of India" is a provision made in the
questions.e: This is a specific provision under Article 51A (Fundamental Duties) added by the 42nd Amendment.

questions.q: The fundamental object of Panchayati Raj system is to ensure which among the following 1️⃣ People's participation in development 2️⃣ Political accountability 3️⃣ Democratic decentralization 4️⃣ Financial mobilization
questions.e: The core objectives are democratic decentralization and people's participation. While political accountability exists, "financial mobilization" is not the *fundamental* object.

questions.q: The ideal of 'Welfare State' in the Indian Constitution is enshrined in its
questions.e: The DPSP (Part IV) aims at establishing a social and economic democracy, which is the hallmark of a Welfare State.

questions.q: There is a Parliamentary System of Government in India because the
o: Lok Sabha is elected directly by the people
Council of Ministers is responsible to the Lok Sabha
questions.e: The most fundamental feature of a parliamentary system is the collective responsibility of the executive to the lower house of the legislature.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ A Bill pending in the Lok Sabha lapses on its prorogation. 2️⃣ A Bill pending in the Rajya Sabha, which has not been passed by the Lok Sabha, shall not lapse on dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
questions.e: Prorogation does not affect pending bills. A bill originating and pending in Rajya Sabha (not yet passed by LS) does not lapse when the Lok Sabha dissolves.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Chief Secretary in a State is appointed by the Governor of that State. 2️⃣ The Chief Secretary in a State has a fixed tenure.
questions.e: The Chief Secretary is appointed by the Chief Minister (expressed in the name of the Governor). There is no fixed tenure for this post.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Gram Nyayalaya Act', which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ As per the Act, Gram Nyayalayas can hear only civil cases and not criminal cases. 2️⃣ The Act allows local social activists as mediators/reconciliators.
questions.e: Gram Nyayalayas have jurisdiction over both criminal and civil cases. The Act explicitly provides for the appointment of social workers as conciliators.

questions.q: The Parliament of India acquires the power to legislate on any item in the State List in the national interest if a resolution to that effect is passed by the
o: Lok Sabha by a majority of not less than two-thirds of its total membership
Rajya Sabha by a majority of not less than two-thirds of its members present and voting
Lok Sabha by a simple majority of its total membership
Rajya Sabha by a simple majority of its total membership
questions.e: Under Article 249, if Rajya Sabha passes such a resolution by a 2/3rd majority of members present and voting, Parliament can legislate on state subjects.

questions.q: Which one of the following objectives is not embodied in the Preamble to the Constitution of India?
questions.e: The Preamble secures to all citizens liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith, and worship. It mentions Justice (social, economic, and political) but does not explicitly use the term "Economic liberty".

questions.q: The mind of the makers of the Constitution of India is reflected in which of the following?
o: The Directive Principles of State Policy
questions.e: The Preamble serves as an introduction to the Constitution and embodies the basic philosophy and fundamental values on which the Constitution is built, thus reflecting the mind of the makers.

questions.q: Which of the following are envisaged by the Right against Exploitation in the Constitution of India? 1️⃣ Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour 2️⃣ Abolition of untouchability 3️⃣ Protection of the interests of minorities 4️⃣ Prohibition of employment of children in factories and mines
questions.e: Articles 23 and 24 cover the Right against Exploitation, specifically prohibiting human trafficking, forced labor, and child labor in hazardous conditions. Untouchability is covered under the Right to Equality (Art 17), and minority interests are covered under Cultural and Educational Rights.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Rights are claims of the citizens against the State.
Rights are privileges of a few citizens against the many.
Rights are privileges which are incorporated in the Constitution of a State.
Rights are claims of the State against the citizens.
questions.e: In a constitutional democracy, Rights are primarily understood as legal and moral claims that citizens have against the State to protect their liberty and dignity.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are true of the Fundamental Duties of an Indian citizen? 1️⃣ A legislative process has been provided to enforce these duties. 2️⃣ They are correlative to legal duties.
questions.e: Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable; the Constitution does not provide a direct legislative process for their enforcement, nor are they strictly correlative to legal duties in a court of law.

questions.q: In the context of India, which one of the following is the correct relationship between Rights and Duties?
o: Rights are personal and hence independent of society and Duties.
Duties, not Rights, are important for the stability of the State.
Rights, not Duties, are important for the advancement of the personality of the citizen.
questions.e: Rights and duties are two sides of the same coin; the enjoyment of one's rights implies the performance of certain duties towards others and the state.

questions.q: Which principle among the following was added to the Directive Principles of State Policy by the 42nd Amendment to the Constitution?
o: Participation of workers in the management of industries
Right to work, education and public assistance
Securing living wage and human conditions of work to workers
Equal pay for equal work for both men and women
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 added Article 43A, which requires the State to take steps to secure the participation of workers in the management of industries.

questions.q: With reference to the Constitution of India, the Directive Principles of State Policy constitute limitations upon 1️⃣ Legislative function. 2️⃣ Executive function.
questions.e: DPSPs are guiding principles for the state to follow; unlike Fundamental Rights, they do not act as legal limitations or prohibitions on legislative or executive functions.

questions.q: For election to the Lok Sabha, a nomination paper can be filed by
o: Any citizen of India whose name appears in the electoral roll of a constituency.
A resident of the constituency from which the election is to be contested.
questions.e: According to the Representation of the People Act, any citizen whose name is in the electoral roll of any constituency can file a nomination, provided they meet the age and other criteria.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ In the election for Lok Sabha or State Assembly, the winning candidate must get at least 50 percent of the votes polled, to be declared elected. 2️⃣ According to the provisions laid down in the Constitution of India, in Lok Sabha, the Speaker's post goes to the majority party and the Deputy Speaker's to the Opposition.
questions.e: India follows the "First Past the Post" system where the candidate with the highest votes wins, regardless of the 50% mark. The convention of the Deputy Speaker coming from the opposition is a parliamentary practice, not a constitutional provision.

questions.q: Right to vote and to be elected in India is a
questions.e: The Right to Vote in India is a constitutional right granted under Article 326 of the Constitution.

questions.q: Which of the following are not necessarily the consequences of the proclamation of the President's rule in a State? 1️⃣ Dissolution of the State Legislative Assembly 2️⃣ Removal of the Council of Ministers in the State 3️⃣ Dissolution of the local bodies
questions.e: When President's Rule is imposed, the Council of Ministers is dismissed, but the Assembly can be either suspended or dissolved. Dissolution of local bodies is not a consequence of Article 356.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not a feature of Indian federalism?
o: There is an independent judiciary in India.
The federating units have been given unequal representation in the Rajya Sabha.
Powers have been clearly divided between the Centre and the States.
It is the result of an agreement among the federating units.
questions.e: Unlike the US federation, the Indian federation is not the result of an agreement among states, and states have no right to secede from the Union.

questions.q: Local self-government can be best explained as an exercise in
questions.e: The primary aim of local self-government (Panchayats and Municipalities) is to decentralize power to the grassroots level and ensure people's participation.

questions.q: The Parliament of India exercises control over the functions of the Council of Ministers through 1️⃣ Adjournment motion 2️⃣ Question hour 3️⃣ Supplementary questions
questions.e: Parliament uses various procedural devices like Question Hour (for information), Supplementary Questions (for follow-up), and Adjournment Motions (to discuss urgent matters) to hold the executive accountable.

questions.q: With reference to the Parliament of India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ A private member's bill is a bill presented by a Member of Parliament who is not elected but only nominated by the President of India. 2️⃣ Recently, a private member's bill has been passed in the Parliament of India for the first time in its history.
questions.e: A private member's bill is any bill introduced by an MP who is not a Minister (elected or nominated). Several private member's bills have been passed in the past, though it is rare.

questions.q: The main advantage of the parliamentary form of government is that
o: It provides continuity of policy and is more efficient.
The executive remains responsible to the legislature.
The head of the government cannot be changed without election.
The executive and legislature work independently.
questions.e: The defining characteristic and main advantage of the parliamentary system is the continuous accountability of the executive to the legislature.

questions.q: Out of the following statements, choose the one that brings out the principle underlying the Cabinet form of Government:
o: A device for strengthening the hands of the head of the Government whose hold over the people is in a state of decline.
A mechanism of parliamentary democracy for ensuring collective responsibility of the Government to the people.
A mechanism for speeding up the activities of the Government whose responsibilities are increasing day by day.
An arrangement for minimizing the criticism against the Government whose responsibilities are complex and hard to carry out to the satisfaction of all.
questions.e: The Cabinet form of government is designed to ensure the collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the legislature (and through it, to the people).

questions.q: In India, Judicial Review implies
o: The power of the Judiciary to review all the legislative enactments before they are assented to by the President.
The power of the Judiciary to question the wisdom of the laws enacted by the Legislatures.
The power of the Judiciary to pronounce upon the constitutionality of laws and executive orders.
The power of the Judiciary to review its own judgements given earlier in similar or different cases.
questions.e: Judicial Review is the power of the courts to examine the actions of the legislative and executive arms of the government and determine if they are consistent with the Constitution.

questions.q: Democracy's superior virtue lies in the fact that it calls into activity
o: The intelligence and character of ordinary men and women.
The methods for strengthening executive leadership.
A superior individual with dynamism and vision.
A band of dedicated party workers.
questions.e: Democracy is valued because it empowers ordinary citizens, encouraging them to participate in governance and develop their civic character.

questions.q: One of the implications of equality in society is the absence of
questions.e: Equality implies that no individual or group should enjoy special privileges that are denied to others in the society.

questions.q: In the federation established by the Government of India Act of 1935, Residuary Powers were given to the
questions.e: Under the 1935 Act, the powers were divided into three lists. Unlike the current Constitution where residuary powers belong to the Parliament, the 1935 Act vested them in the Governor-General.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Aadhaar card can be used as a proof of citizenship or domicile. 2️⃣ Once issued, Aadhaar number cannot be deactivated or omitted by the Issuing Authority.
questions.e: The Supreme Court and UIDAI have clarified that Aadhaar is a proof of identity and residence, not citizenship. The authority also has powers to deactivate numbers in cases of fraud or multiple enrollments.

questions.q: Right to Privacy is protected as an intrinsic part of Right to Life and Personal Liberty. Which of the following in the Constitution of India correctly and appropriately imply the above statement?
o: Article 21 and the freedoms guaranteed in Part III
Article 24 and the provisions under the 44th Amendment to the Constitution
Article 17 and the Directive Principles of State Policy in Part IV
Article 14 and the provisions under the 42nd Amendment to the Constitution
questions.e: In the KS Puttaswamy case (2017), the Supreme Court declared Right to Privacy a fundamental right under Article 21 and Part III of the Constitution.

questions.q: With reference to the election of the President of India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The value of the vote of each MLA varies from State to State. 2️⃣ The value of the vote of MPs of the Lok Sabha is more than the value of the vote of MPs of the Rajya Sabha.
questions.e: The MLA vote value is based on state population (1971 census), so it varies by state. However, the vote value of all elected MPs (LS and RS) is equalized and constant.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ No criminal proceedings shall be instituted against the Governor of a State in any court during his term of office. 2️⃣ The emoluments and allowances of the Governor of a State shall not be diminished during his term of office.
questions.e: Article 361 provides immunity to the Governor from criminal proceedings during their term. Additionally, Article 158(4) ensures their financial benefits cannot be reduced to their disadvantage while in office.

questions.q: Which of the following Parliamentary Committees scrutinizes and reports to the House whether the powers to make regulations, rules, sub-rules, by-laws, etc. conferred by the Constitution or delegated by the Parliament are being properly exercised by the Executive within the scope of such delegation?
questions.e: The Committee on Subordinate Legislation examines whether the executive is staying within the bounds of the "delegated legislation" granted by the Parliament.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly shall vacate his/her office if he/she ceases to be a member of the Assembly. 2️⃣ Whenever the Legislative Assembly is dissolved, the Speaker shall vacate his/her office immediately.
questions.e: While the Speaker must be a member of the House, the Constitution specifies that the Speaker does not vacate office upon dissolution; they continue until immediately before the first meeting of the new Assembly.

questions.q: If the President of India exercises his power as provided under Article 356 of the Constitution in respect of a particular State, then
o: Article 19 is suspended in that State.
the Assembly of the State is automatically dissolved.
the President can make laws relating to that State.
the powers of the Legislature of that State shall be exercisable by or under the authority of the Parliament.
questions.e: Under President's Rule, the Parliament assumes the legislative powers of the state. The Assembly may be suspended rather than dissolved, and Article 19 is only suspended during a National Emergency (Art 358).

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Parliament of India can place a particular law in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution of India. 2️⃣ The validity of a law placed in the Ninth Schedule cannot be examined by any court and no judgement can be made on it.
questions.e: While Parliament can add laws to the Ninth Schedule, the Supreme Court ruled in the I.R. Coelho case (2007) that laws added after April 24, 1973, are open to judicial review if they violate the basic structure.

questions.q: Which of the following reflects the most appropriate relationship between law and liberty?
o: If there are no laws, there is no liberty.
If there is liberty, laws have to be made by the people.
If laws are changed too often, liberty is in danger.
if there are more laws, there is less liberty.
questions.e: As John Locke famously noted, "where there is no law, there is no freedom," because law protects individuals from the arbitrary interference of others.

questions.q: Which of the following are regarded as the main features of the "Rule of Law"? 1️⃣ Limitation of powers 2️⃣ Equality before law 3️⃣ People's responsibility to the Government 4️⃣ Liberty and civil rights
questions.e: Rule of law (A.V. Dicey) emphasizes the absence of arbitrary power, equality before the law, and the protection of individual rights. "Responsibility to the government" is not a standard feature.

questions.q: Regarding Money Bill, which of the following statement is not correct?
o: A bill shall be deemed to be a Money Bill if it contains only provisions relating to imposition, abolition, remission, alteration or regulation of any tax.
A Money Bill deals with the regulation of borrowing of money or giving of any guarantee by the Government of India.
A Money Bill has provisions for the custody of the Consolidated Fund of India or the Contingency Fund of India.
A Money bill is concerned with the appropriation of moneys out of the Contingency Fund of India.
questions.e: Money Bills deal with the *Consolidated* Fund of India (Art 110). Appropriation from the *Contingency* Fund is not the primary defining feature of a Money Bill.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India safeguards one's right to marry the person of one's choice?
questions.e: The Supreme Court (Hadiya case) held that the right to marry a person of choice is an integral part of Article 21 (Right to Life and Liberty).

questions.q: Under which schedule of the Constitution of India can the transfer of tribal land to private parties for mining be declared null and void?
questions.e: The Fifth Schedule deals with the administration of Scheduled Areas. In the Samatha vs. State of Andhra Pradesh case, the court ruled that such transfers violate the protections for tribal land.

questions.q: The Ninth Schedule was introduced in the Constitution of India during the prime ministership of
questions.e: The Ninth Schedule was added by the 1st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951, while Jawaharlal Nehru was Prime Minister.

questions.q: Which one of the following suggested that the Governor should be an eminent person from outside the State and should be a detached figure without intense political links?
o: National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (2000)
questions.e: The Sarkaria Commission on Centre-State relations recommended these criteria to ensure the Governor remains a neutral constitutional head.

questions.q: Rajya Sabha has equal powers with Lok Sabha in
o: the matter of creating new All India Services
questions.e: Constitution Amendment Bills must be passed by both Houses independently with no provision for a joint sitting. Rajya Sabha has *greater* power in creating All India Services (Art 312) and *lesser* power in money matters.

questions.q: In India, separation of judiciary from the executive is enjoined by
o: a Directive Principle of State Policy
questions.e: Article 50 of the Directive Principles of State Policy mandates the State to take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in public services.

questions.q: Along with the Budget, the Finance Minister also places other documents before the Parliament which include 'The Macro Economic Framework Statement'. This document is presented because this is mandated by
o: Provisions of the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003
Article 112 and Article 110(1) of the Constitution of India
Article 113 of the Constitution of India
questions.e: The FRBM Act, 2003 requires the government to place the Macro-Economic Framework Statement and the Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement before Parliament along with the annual budget.

questions.q: With reference to the Union Government, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ N. Gopalaswamy Iyengar Committee suggested that a minister and a secretary be designated solely for pursuing the subject of administrative reform and promoting it. 2️⃣ In 1970, the Department of Personnel was constituted on the recommendation of the Administrative Reforms Commission, 1966, and this was placed under the Prime Minister's charge.
questions.e: The N. Gopalaswamy Iyengar Committee (1949) focused on the reorganization of government machinery but did not suggest a specific minister for reforms. The Department of Personnel was indeed established in 1970 following the ARC's recommendation and placed under the Cabinet Secretariat (PM's charge).

questions.q: 'Right to Privacy' is protected under which Article of the Constitution of India?
questions.e: The Supreme Court, in the Justice K.S. Puttaswamy case, declared that the Right to Privacy is an intrinsic part of the Right to Life and Personal Liberty under Article 21.

questions.q: With reference to India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Judicial custody means an accused is in the custody of the concerned magistrate and such accused is locked up in police station, not in jail. 2️⃣ During judicial custody, the police officer in charge of the case is not allowed to interrogate the suspect without the approval of the court.
questions.e: Judicial custody means the accused is in the custody of a Magistrate and lodged in jail, not a police station. Interrogation during this period requires specific court permission.

questions.q: With reference to India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ When a prisoner makes out a sufficient case, parole cannot be denied to such prisoner because it becomes a matter of his/her right. 2️⃣ State Governments have their own Prisoners Release on Parole Rules.
questions.e: Parole is a discretionary grant and not a fundamental right of the prisoner. Since "Prisons" is a State subject, State Governments have the authority to frame their own parole rules.

questions.q: At the national level, which ministry is the nodal agency to ensure effective implementation of the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
questions.e: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs is the designated nodal agency for the implementation of the Forest Rights Act (2006) at the national level.

questions.q: Which one of the following in Indian polity is an essential feature that indicates that it is federal in character?
o: The independence of judiciary is safeguarded.
The Union Cabinet can have elected representatives from regional parties.
The Union Legislature has elected representatives from constituent units.
The Fundamental Rights are enforceable by Courts of Law.
questions.e: An independent judiciary is a key federal feature as it acts as an arbiter in disputes between the Centre and the States.

questions.q: Which one of the following best defines the term 'State'?
o: A number of persons who have been living in a definite territory for a very long time with their own culture, tradition and government
A politically organized people of a definite territory and possessing an authority to govern them, maintain law and order, protect their natural rights and safeguard their means of sustenance
A society permanently living in a definite territory with a central authority, an executive responsible to the central authority and an independent judiciary
A community of persons permanently occupying a definite territory independent of external control and possessing an organized government
questions.e: In political science, a 'State' is traditionally defined by four elements: population, territory, government, and sovereignty (independence from external control).

questions.q: With reference to Indian judiciary, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Any retired judge of the Supreme Court of India can be called back to sit and act as a Supreme Court judge by the Chief Justice of India with prior permission of the President of India. 2️⃣ A High Court in India has the power to review its own judgement as the Supreme Court does.
questions.e: Article 128 allows the CJI to request a retired SC judge to sit and act as a judge with the President's consent. High Courts, as Courts of Record, have inherent powers to review their own judgements.

questions.q: With reference to India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ There is only one citizenship and one domicile. 2️⃣ A citizen by birth only can become the Head of State. 3️⃣ A foreigner once granted the citizenship cannot be deprived of it under any circumstances.
questions.e: India provides for single citizenship; unlike the USA, there is no separate state domicile for citizenship. In India, both natural-born and naturalized citizens can become the Head of State. Citizenship can be deprived in certain cases like fraud or disloyalty.

questions.q: Under the Indian Constitution, concentration of wealth violates
o: the Directive Principles of State Policy
questions.e: Article 39(c) of the Directive Principles of State Policy explicitly directs the State to ensure that the operation of the economic system does not result in the concentration of wealth.

questions.q: What is the position of the Right to Property in India?
o: Fundamental Right available to citizens only
Neither Fundamental Right nor legal right
Legal right available to citizens only
Legal right available to any person
questions.e: Originally a Fundamental Right, the 44th Amendment moved it to Article 300A, making it a legal right available to any "person" (not just citizens).

questions.q: What was the exact constitutional status of India on 26th January, 1950?
o: A Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic
questions.e: In 1950, the Preamble described India as a "Sovereign Democratic Republic". The terms "Socialist" and "Secular" were added later by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.

questions.q: Constitutional government means
o: a representative government of a nation with federal structure
a government limited by the terms of the Constitution
a government whose Head enjoys real powers
a government whose Head enjoys nominal powers
questions.e: The essence of constitutionalism is "limited government," where the powers of the state are defined and restricted by a constitution to protect individual liberty.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Pursuant to the report of H.N. Sanyal Committee, the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 was passed. 2️⃣ The Constitution of India empowers the Supreme Court and the High Courts to punish for contempt of themselves. 3️⃣ The Constitution of India defines Civil Contempt and Criminal Contempt. 4️⃣ In India, the Parliament is vested with the powers to make laws on Contempt of Court.
questions.e: The 1971 Act followed the Sanyal Committee report. Articles 129 and 215 empower the SC and HC to punish for contempt. The definitions of Civil/Criminal contempt are in the 1971 Act, not the Constitution. Parliament can legislate on this under the Concurrent List.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ A bill amending the Constitution requires a prior recommendation of the President of India. 2️⃣ When a Constitution Amendment Bill is presented to the President of India, it is obligatory for the President of India to give his/her assent. 3️⃣ A Constitution Amendment Bill must be passed by both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha by a special majority and there is no provision for joint sitting.
questions.e: No prior recommendation is needed for an amendment bill. The 24th Amendment made it obligatory for the President to give assent. Both houses must pass it separately by special majority as per Article 368.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Constitution of India classifies the ministers into four ranks viz. Cabinet Minister, Minister of State with Independent Charge, Minister of State and Deputy Minister. 2️⃣ The total number of ministers in the Union Government, including the Prime Minister, shall not exceed 15 percent of the total number of members in the Lok Sabha.
questions.e: The Constitution does not classify ranks of ministers; this is based on parliamentary convention. The 15% limit was added by the 91st Amendment Act, 2003.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are the exclusive power(s) of Lok Sabha? 1️⃣ To ratify the declaration of Emergency 2️⃣ To pass a motion of no-confidence against the Council of Ministers 3️⃣ To impeach the President of India
questions.e: Both houses must ratify Emergency and participate in impeachment. However, a No-Confidence Motion can only be introduced and passed in the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: With reference to anti-defection law in India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The law specifies that a nominated legislator cannot join any political party within six months of being appointed to the House. 2️⃣ The law does not provide any time-frame within which the presiding officer has to decide a defection case.
questions.e: A nominated member *can* join a party within six months; they are disqualified if they join *after* six months. The Supreme Court has noted that the Tenth Schedule provides no specific timeline for the Presiding Officer's decision.

questions.q: With reference to the writs issued by the Courts in India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Mandamus will not lie against a private organisation unless it is entrusted with a public duty. 2️⃣ Mandamus will not lie against a Company even though it may be a Government Company. 3️⃣ Any public minded person can be a petitioner to move the Court to obtain the writ of Quo Warranto.
questions.e: Mandamus is used for public duties, regardless of the private nature of the body. It *can* lie against government companies. Quo Warranto does not require the petitioner to be the aggrieved party.

questions.q: In essence, what does 'Due Process of Law' mean?
questions.e: While the Indian Constitution originally used "procedure established by law," the Supreme Court (Maneka Gandhi case) interpreted it to include 'Due Process,' which aligns with natural justice and fairness.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: Statement-I: In India, prisons are managed by State Governments with their own rules and regulations for the day-to-day administration of prisons. Statement-II: In India, prisons are governed by the Prisons Act, 1894 which expressly kept the subject of prisons in the control of Provincial Governments.
o: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
questions.e: Under the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution, 'Prisons' is a State subject. The Prisons Act of 1894 remains the primary legislation that historically and legally vested the management and control of prisons in the hands of the provincial (now state) governments.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements best reflects the Chief purpose of the "Constitution" of a country?
o: It secures social justice, social equality and social security.
It defines and limits the powers of government.
It enables the creation of political offices and a government.
It determines the objective for the making of necessary laws.
questions.e: While a constitution performs many functions, its fundamental purpose in a liberal democracy is to establish a framework that defines and, more importantly, limits the powers of the government to prevent arbitrary rule and protect individual rights.

questions.q: In India, which one of the following Constitutional Amendments was widely believed to be enacted to overcome the judicial interpretations of the Fundamental Rights?
questions.e: The 1st Constitutional Amendment Act (1951) was primarily enacted to bypass judicial hurdles related to zamindari abolition and land reforms, as well as to address interpretations regarding freedom of speech and the right to practice any profession.

questions.q: Consider the following organizations/bodies in India: 1️⃣ The National Commission for Backward Classes 2️⃣ The National Human Rights Commission 3️⃣ The National Law Commission 4️⃣ The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission. How many of the above are constitutional bodies?
questions.e: Only the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) is a constitutional body, having been granted that status via the 102nd Amendment Act (Article 338B). The others are either statutory bodies (NHRC, NCDRC) or executive advisory bodies (Law Commission).

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ If the election of the President of India is declared void by the Supreme Court of India, all acts done by him/her in the performance of duties of his/her office of President before the date of decision become invalid. 2️⃣ Election for the post of the President of India can be postponed on the ground that some Legislative Assemblies have been dissolved and elections are yet to take place. 3️⃣ When a Bill is presented to the President of India, the Constitution prescribes time limits within which he/she has to declare his/her assent. How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is wrong because acts done by the President remain valid even if the election is later declared void. Statement 2 is wrong because a vacancy in the electoral college (like a dissolved assembly) is not a ground to postpone the election. Statement 3 is wrong because the Constitution does not prescribe a specific time limit for the President to give assent (leading to the "pocket veto").

questions.q: With reference to Finance Bill and Money Bill in the Indian Parliament, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ When the Lok Sabha transmits Finance Bill to the Rajya Sabha, it can amend or reject the Bill. 2️⃣ When the Lok Sabha transmits Money Bill to the Rajya Sabha, it cannot amend or reject the Bill, it can only make recommendations. 3️⃣ In the case of disagreement between the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, there is no joint sitting for Money Bill, but a joint sitting becomes necessary for Finance Bill. How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 and 2 are correct; Rajya Sabha has restricted powers over Money Bills but has regular powers (amend/reject) over Finance Bills that are not exclusively Money Bills. Statement 3 is partially correct; while there is no joint sitting for a Money Bill, a joint sitting is *possible* for a Finance Bill but not always "necessary" as a default mandate.

questions.q: With reference to 'Scheduled Areas' in India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Within a State, the notification of an area as Scheduled Area takes place through an Order of the President. 2️⃣ The largest administrative unit forming the Scheduled Area is the District and the lowest is the cluster of villages in the Block. 3️⃣ The Chief Ministers of the concerned States are required to submit annual reports to the Union Home Ministry on the administration of Scheduled Areas in the States. How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct (Art. 244). Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because the *Governor*, not the Chief Minister, is responsible for submitting reports to the President/Union Government.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: Statement-I: The Supreme Court of India has held in some judgements that the reservation policies made under Article 16(4) of the Constitution of India would be limited by Article 335 for maintenance of efficiency of administration. Statement-II: Article 335 of the Constitution of India defines the term 'efficiency of administration'.
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
questions.e: Statement I is correct as the SC has linked Art. 16(4) with Art. 335 in various cases (e.g., Indra Sawhney). Statement II is incorrect because the Constitution does *not* define 'efficiency of administration'.

questions.q: By which one of the following Acts was the Governor General of Bengal designated as the Governor General of India?
questions.e: The Charter Act of 1833 elevated the Governor-General of Bengal to the Governor-General of India and vested in him all civil and military power.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ According to the Constitution of India, the Central Government has a duty to protect States from internal disturbances. 2️⃣ The Constitution of India exempts the States from providing legal counsel to a person being held for preventive detention. 3️⃣ According to the Prevention of Terrorism Act, 2002, confession of the accused before the police cannot be used as evidence. How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct under Article 355. Statement 2 is correct as Article 22 specifically excludes persons under preventive detention from certain procedural rights. Statement 3 is incorrect; POTA (since repealed) actually allowed confessions before a high-ranking police officer as evidence under certain conditions.

questions.q: A Writ of Prohibition is an order issued by the Supreme Court or High Courts to:
o: the lower court prohibiting continuation of proceedings in a case.
a government officer prohibiting him from taking a particular action.
the Parliament/Legislative Assembly to pass a law on Prohibition.
the Government prohibiting it from following an unconstitutional policy.
questions.e: The writ of Prohibition is issued by a higher court to a lower court or quasi-judicial body to prevent it from exceeding its jurisdiction or acting contrary to natural justice.

questions.q: Who was the Provisional President of the Constituent Assembly before Dr. Rajendra Prasad took over?
questions.e: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha, the oldest member, was elected as the temporary/provisional President of the Constituent Assembly following the French practice during its first meeting on December 9, 1946.

questions.q: The North Eastern Council (NEC) was established by the North Eastern Council Act, 1971. Subsequent to the amendment of NEC Act in 2002, the Council comprises which of the following members? 1️⃣ Governor of the Constituent State 2️⃣ Chief Minister of the Constituent State 3️⃣ Three Members to be nominated by the President of India 4️⃣ The Home Minister of India
questions.e: Following the 2002 amendment, the NEC consists of the Governors and Chief Ministers of the eight member states (including Sikkim) and three members nominated by the President. The Union Home Minister acts as the ex-officio Chairman but is generally considered distinct from the core constituent "council members" in this specific exam context.

questions.q: With reference to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, consider the following statements: While any resolution for the removal of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is under consideration 1️⃣ He/She shall not preside. 2️⃣ He/She shall not have the right to speak. 3️⃣ He/She shall not be entitled to vote on the resolution in the first instance.
questions.e: Under Article 96, when a removal resolution is active, the Speaker cannot preside but has the right to speak and take part in proceedings. They can vote in the first instance on such a resolution, but notably, they cannot vote in the case of an equality of votes (casting vote).

questions.q: How many Delimitation Commissions have been constituted by the Government of India till December 2023?
questions.e: Four Delimitation Commissions have been set up under the Acts of 1952, 1962, 1972, and 2002.

questions.q: Which reference to the Indian polity, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ An Ordinance can amend any Central Act. 1️⃣1️⃣ An Ordinance can abridge a Fundamental Right. 2️⃣1️⃣ An Ordinance can come into effect from a back date. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: An Ordinance has the same force and effect as an Act of Parliament (Art. 123), meaning it can amend Acts and be retrospective. However, like any law, an Ordinance cannot abridge or take away Fundamental Rights.

questions.q: With reference to the Indian polity, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Governor of a State is not answerable to any court for the exercise and performance of the powers and duties of his/her office. 2️⃣ No criminal proceedings shall be instituted or continued against the Governor during his/her term of office. 3️⃣ Members of a State Legislature are not liable to any proceedings in any court in respect of anything said within the House. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 and 2 represent the constitutional immunities of the Governor under Article 361. Statement 3 represents the parliamentary privileges of state legislators under Article 194.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Constitution of India explicitly mentions that in certain spheres the Governor of a State acts in his/her own discretion. 2️⃣ The President of India can, of his/her own, reserve a bill passed by a State Legislature for his/her consideration without it being forwarded by the Governor of the State concerned. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Unlike the President, the Constitution explicitly mentions discretionary powers for the Governor (Art. 163). However, the President only receives bills for consideration if they are reserved and forwarded by the Governor.

questions.q: Consider the following statements with regard to pardoning power of the President of India: 1️⃣ The exercise of this power by the President can be subjected to limited judicial review. 2️⃣ The President can exercise this power without the advice of the Central Government. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Supreme Court (e.g., in Epuru Sudhakar) held that the pardoning power is subject to limited judicial review for grounds like malafide or arbitrariness. However, the President must exercise this power on the advice of the Union Cabinet, not independently.

questions.q: Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Bharatiya Jana Sangh: Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee 2️⃣ Socialist Party: C. Rajagopalachari 3️⃣ Congress for Democracy: Jagjivan Ram 4️⃣ Swatantra Party: Acharya Narendra Dev. How many of the above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct. Pair 2 is incorrect (Socialist Party was led by leaders like JP Narayan/Narendra Dev) and Pair 4 is incorrect (Swatantra Party was founded by C. Rajagopalachari).

questions.q: Under the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, bamboo is a minor forest produce. 1️⃣ The Scheduled Tribes and other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 allows ownership of minor forest produce to forest dwellers.
questions.e: In 2017, the Indian Forest Act was amended to remove bamboo from the category of 'tree', allowing for its felling and transport. The 2006 Act (FRA) specifically defines bamboo as a minor forest produce and grants ownership rights to forest-dwelling communities.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The 44th Amendment to the Constitution of India introduced an Article placing the election of the Prime Minister beyond judicial review. 2️⃣ The Supreme Court of India struck down the 99th Amendment to the Constitution of India as being violative of the independence of judiciary.
questions.e: The 39th Amendment, not the 44th, sought to place the PM's election beyond review. The Supreme Court struck down the 99th Amendment (NJAC) in 2015 to protect judicial independence.

questions.q: With reference to the Constitution of India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ No High Court shall have the jurisdiction to declare any central law to be constitutionally invalid. 2️⃣ An amendment to the Constitution of India cannot be called into question by the Supreme Court of India.
questions.e: High Courts have the power to strike down central laws within their jurisdiction. Constitutional amendments can be challenged in the Supreme Court if they violate the "Basic Structure".

questions.q: With reference to the constitution of India, prohibitions or limitations or provisions contained in ordinary laws cannot act as prohibitions or limitations on the constitutional powers under Article 142. It could mean which one of the following?
o: The Supreme Court of India is not constrained in the exercise of its powers by laws made by the parliament.
In the event of grave financial crises in the country, the President of India can declare Financial Emergency without the counsel from the cabinet.
State Legislatures can not make laws on certain matters without the concurrence of the Union legislature.
The decisions taken by the Election Commission of India while discharging its duties can not be challenged in any court of law.
questions.e: Article 142 grants the Supreme Court the power to pass any order necessary for doing "complete justice," and this power is not restricted by ordinary statutory laws.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The motion to impeach a judge of the Supreme Court of India cannot be rejected by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha as per the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968. 2️⃣ The constitution of India defines and gives details of what constitutes 'incapacity and proved misbehaviour' of the judges of the Supreme Court of India. 3️⃣ The details of the process of the impeachment of the judges of the Supreme Court of India are given in the judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968. 4️⃣ If the motion of the impeachment of a judge is taken up for voting, the law requires the motion to be backed by each house of the parliament and supported by a majority of total membership of that house and by not less than two-thirds of total members of that House present and voting.
questions.e: The Speaker has the discretion to admit or refuse an impeachment motion. The Constitution does not define 'incapacity' or 'misbehaviour'; however, the 1968 Act provides the procedural details, and the 2/3rd majority requirement is mandatory.

questions.q: The Parliament (Prevention of Disqualification) Act, 1959 exempts several posts from disqualification on the grounds of 'Office of Profit'. 1️⃣ The above-mentioned Act was amended five times. 2️⃣ The term 'Office of Profit' is well-defined in the Constitution of India.
questions.e: The 1959 Act has been amended several times to protect members from disqualification. Notably, the term 'Office of Profit' is mentioned but not defined anywhere in the Constitution.

questions.q: With reference to the Legislative Assembly of a State in India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Governor makes a customary address to members of the house at the commencement of the first session of the year. 2️⃣ When a State Legislature does not have a rule on the particular matter, it follows the Lok Sabha rule on that matter.
questions.e: Article 176 provides for the Governor's special address. While state assemblies often model their rules after the Lok Sabha, it is not a mandatory constitutional requirement to follow them automatically.

questions.q: In the context of polity, which one of the following would you accept as the most appropriate definition of liberty?
o: Protection against the tyranny of political rulers
Opportunity to do whatever one likes
questions.e: While liberty involves the absence of restraint, its positive and most complete definition in a political context is providing the environment for individuals to achieve their full potential.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about 'the Charter Act of 1813': 1️⃣ It ended the trade monopoly of the East India Company in India except for trade in tea and trade with China. 2️⃣ It asserted the sovereignty of the British Crown over the Indian territories held by the Company. 3️⃣ The revenues of India were now controlled by the British Parliament.
questions.e: The 1813 Act broke the Company's monopoly (except tea/China) and explicitly stated the Crown's sovereignty. However, total Parliamentary control over revenues came much later, after 1858.

questions.q: In India, which of the following review the independent regulators in sectors like telecommunications, insurance, electricity etc.? 1️⃣ Ad Hoc Committees set up by the Parliament 2️⃣ Parliamentary Department Related Standing Committees 3️⃣ Finance Commission 4️⃣ Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission 5️⃣ NITI Aayog
questions.e: Independent regulators are primarily held accountable through Parliamentary oversight, specifically through Standing Committees and Ad Hoc committees.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Aadhaar metadata cannot be stored more than three months. 2️⃣ State cannot enter into any contract with private corporations for sharing of Aadhaar data. 3️⃣ Aadhaar is mandatory for obtaining insurance products. 4️⃣ Aadhaar is mandatory for getting benefits funded out of the Consolidated Fund of India.
questions.e: The Supreme Court struck down the use of Aadhaar by private entities. It is mandatory for welfare schemes funded by the Consolidated Fund of India, but not for insurance or bank accounts.

questions.q: With reference to the funds under Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLADS), which of the following statements are correct? 1️⃣ MPLADS funds must be used to create durable assets like physical infrastructure for health, education, etc. 2️⃣ A specified portion of each MP's fund must benefit SC/ST populations. 3️⃣ MPLADS funds are sanctioned on yearly basis and the unused funds cannot be carried forward to the next year. 4️⃣ The district authority must inspect at least 10% of all works under implementation every year.
questions.e: MPLADS funds are non-lapsable, meaning unused funds *can* be carried forward. The other statements regarding SC/ST allocation and mandatory inspection are correct.

questions.q: Which one of the following categories of Fundamental Rights incorporates protection against untouchability as a form of discrimination?
questions.e: Article 17, which abolishes untouchability, falls under the broad category of the 'Right to Equality' (Articles 14–18).

questions.q: Other than the Fundamental Rights, which of the following parts of the Constitution of India reflect/reflects the principles and provisions of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948)? 1️⃣ Preamble 2️⃣ Directive Principles of State Policy 3️⃣ Fundamental Duties
questions.e: The values of the UDHR are deeply embedded across the Preamble, the DPSP (social/economic rights), and Fundamental Duties (civic responsibilities).

questions.q: In India, Legal Services Authorities provide free legal services to which of the following type of citizens? 1️⃣ Person with an annual income of less than ₹1,00,000 2️⃣ Transgender with an annual income of less than ₹2,00,000 3️⃣ Member of Other Backward Classes (OBC) with an annual income of less than ₹3,00,000 4️⃣ All Senior Citizens
questions.e: Income limits for legal aid vary by state, but broadly target lower-income individuals and vulnerable groups. Senior citizens are not automatically eligible regardless of income unless specified by state rules.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Constitution of India defines its 'basic structure' in terms of federalism, secularism, fundamental rights and democracy. 2️⃣ The Constitution of India provides for 'judicial review' to safeguard the citizens' liberties and to preserve the ideals on which the Constitution is based.
questions.e: The term 'Basic Structure' is a judicial innovation and is not defined in the Constitution. Judicial review is provided through various Articles (like 13, 32, 226) to protect constitutional integrity.

questions.q: One common agreement between Gandhism and Marxism is
o: the final goal of a stateless Society
questions.e: Both ideologies ultimately envision a future where the state as an instrument of power ceases to exist, although their methods to reach this "stateless society" differ vastly.

questions.q: The Preamble to the Constitution of India is
o: a part of the Constitution but has no legal effect independently of other parts
not a part of the Constitution and has no legal effect either
a part of the Constitution but has no legal effect
a part of the Constitution and has the same legal effect as any other part
questions.e: The Supreme Court (Kesavananda Bharati case) held the Preamble is a part of the Constitution. However, it cannot be enforced in a court of law on its own without reference to other specific provisions.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ According to the Constitution of India, a person who is eligible to vote can be made a minister in a State for six months even if he/she is not a member of the Legislature of that State. 2️⃣ According to the Representation of People Act, 1951, a person convicted of a criminal offence and sentenced to imprisonment for five years is permanently disqualified from contesting an election even after his release from prison.
questions.e: A person must be at least 25 years old to be a minister, whereas the voting age is 18. Disqualification under the RPA for a 5-year sentence lasts for the duration of the sentence plus an additional 6 years, not permanently.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The President of India can summon a session of the Parliament at such place as he/she thinks fit. 2️⃣ The Constitution of India provides for three sessions of the Parliament in a year, but it is not mandatory to conduct all three sessions. 3️⃣ There is no minimum number of days that the Parliament is required to meet in a year.
questions.e: Article 85 allows the President to summon Parliament. The Constitution only mandates that 6 months must not intervene between sessions; it does not specify "three sessions" or a "minimum number of days".

questions.q: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms of 1919 recommended granting voting rights to all the women above the age of 21. 1️⃣ The Government of India Act of 1935 gave women reserved seats in legislature.
questions.e: The 1919 Act allowed provincial legislatures to decide on women's suffrage but did not grant it to all. The 1935 Act introduced reserved seats for women.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ As regards legislation, the British Parliament is supreme or sovereign but in India, the power of the Parliament to legislate is limited. 2️⃣ In India, matters related to the constitutionality of the Amendment of an Act of the Parliament are referred to the Constitution Bench by the Supreme Court.
questions.e: Unlike the UK, Indian Parliament is limited by a written Constitution and judicial review. Article 145(3) requires a minimum of 5 judges (Constitution Bench) to decide cases involving substantial questions of constitutional interpretation.

questions.q: With reference to India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Judicial custody means an accused is in the custody of the concerned magistrate and such accused is locked up in police station, not in jail. 2️⃣ During judicial custody, the police officer in charge of the case is not allowed to interrogate the suspect without the approval of the court.
questions.e: In judicial custody, the person is held in jail under the magistrate's authority. Police need court permission to interrogate a person in judicial custody.

questions.q: With reference to India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ When a prisoner makes out a sufficient case, parole cannot be denied to such prisoner because it becomes a matter of his/her right. 2️⃣ State Governments have their own Prisoners Release on Parole Rules.
questions.e: Parole is a privilege, not a right. Because prisons are a State subject, each state has its own specific rules for parole.

questions.q: A legislation which confers on the executive or administrative authority an unguided and uncontrolled discretionary power in the matter of application of law violates which one of the following Articles of the Constitution of India?
questions.e: Arbitrary and unguided power is the antithesis of the 'Rule of Law' and 'Equality before Law' guaranteed under Article 14.

questions.q: Which one of the following factors constitutes the best safeguard of liberty in a liberal democracy?
questions.e: Separation of powers (Executive, Legislature, Judiciary) prevents the concentration of power and ensures a system of checks and balances to protect individual liberty.

questions.q: In the Government of India Act 1919, the functions of Provincial Government were divided into "Reserved" and "Transferred" subjects. Which of the following were treated as "Reserved" subjects? 1️⃣ Administration of Justice 2️⃣ Local Self-Government 3️⃣ Land Revenue 4️⃣ Police
questions.e: Under Dyarchy, vital subjects like Justice, Police, and Revenue were "Reserved" for the Governor, while nation-building subjects like Local Self-Government were "Transferred" to ministers.

questions.q: If a particular area is brought under the Fifth Schedule of the Constitution of India, which one of the following statements best reflects the consequence of it?
o: The State having such areas would be declared a Special Category State.
This would prevent the transfer of land of tribal people to non-tribal people.
This would create a local self-governing body in that area.
This would convert that area into a Union Territory.
questions.e: The primary intent of the Fifth Schedule is to protect the interests of tribes, particularly by preventing their land from being alienated to non-tribals.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The National Commission for Backward Classes 2️⃣ The National Human Rights Commission 3️⃣ The National Law Commission 4️⃣ The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission. How many of the above are constitutional bodies?
questions.e: Only the NCBC is constitutional. The Human Rights and Consumer commissions are statutory, and the Law Commission is an executive body.

questions.q: With reference to the Finance Bill and Money Bill in the Indian Parliament, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ When the Lok Sabha transmits Finance Bill to the Rajya Sabha, it can amend or reject the Bill. 2️⃣ When the Lok Sabha transmits Money Bill to the Rajya Sabha, it cannot amend or reject the Bill, it can only make recommendations. 3️⃣ In the case of disagreement between the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, there is no joint sitting for Money Bill, but a joint sitting becomes necessary for Finance Bill. How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 and 2 are true based on legislative powers of Rajya Sabha. Statement 3 is incorrect because while there is no joint sitting for a Money Bill, a joint sitting for a Finance Bill is an *option* in case of deadlock, not a "necessity".

questions.q: With reference to 'Scheduled Areas' in India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Within a State, the notification of an area as Scheduled Area takes place through an Order of the President. 2️⃣ The largest administrative unit forming the Scheduled Area is the District and the lowest is the cluster of villages in the Block. 3️⃣ The Chief Ministers of the concerned States are required to submit annual reports to the Union Home Ministry on the administration of Scheduled Areas in the States. How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: The notification is done by the President. The administrative units listed are correct. However, it is the *Governor* who must report on the administration of Scheduled Areas.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: Statement-I: The Supreme Court of India has held in some judgements that the reservation policies made under Article 16(4) of the Constitution of India would be limited by Article 335 for maintenance of efficiency of administration. Statement-II: Article 335 of the Constitution of India defines the term 'efficiency of administration'.
o: Both Statement-1 and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-i is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-1
Statement-l is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Article 335 mandates considering administrative efficiency, but it does *not* provide a definition for the term.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ According to the Constitution of India, the Central Government has a duty to protect States from internal disturbances. 2️⃣ The Constitution of India exempts the States from providing legal counsel to a person being held for preventive detention. 3️⃣ According to the Prevention of Terrorism Act, 2002, confession of the accused before the police cannot be used as evidence. How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct (Art 355). Statement 2 is correct (Art 22). Statement 3 is incorrect as POTA allowed certain confessions as evidence.

questions.q: Consider the following statements in respect of election to the President of India: 1️⃣ The members nominated to either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assemblies of States are also eligible to be included in the Electoral College. 2️⃣ Higher the number of elective Assembly seats, higher is the value of vote of each MLA of that State. 3️⃣ The value of vote of each MLA of Madhya Pradesh is greater than that of Kerala. 4️⃣ The value of vote of each MLA of Puducherry is higher than that of Arunachal Pradesh. How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only elected members can vote for the President. Vote value is based on population ratios, not just the number of seats. Only statement 4 is correct based on the 1971 population data ratios.

questions.q: Consider the following statements in respect of the Constitution Day: Statement-I: The Constitution Day is celebrated on 26th November every year to promote constitutional values among citizens. Statement-II: On 26th November, 1949, the Constituent Assembly of India set up a Drafting Committee under the Chairmanship of Dr. B. R. Ambedkar to prepare a Draft Constitution of India.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-l is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
questions.e: Constitution Day marks the *adoption* of the Constitution. The Drafting Committee was actually set up on August 29, 1947.

questions.q: With reference to Home Guards, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Home Guards are raised under the Home Guards Act and Rules of the Central Government. 2️⃣ The role of the Home Guards is to serve as an auxiliary force to the police in maintenance of internal security. 3️⃣ To prevent infiltration on the international border/coastal areas, the Border Wing Home Guards Battalions have been raised in some States. How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Home Guards are governed by *State* acts, not Central. The other two roles listed are accurate.

questions.q: The Constitution (71st Amendment) Act, 1992 amends the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution to include which of the following languages? 1️⃣ Konkani 2️⃣ Manipuri 3️⃣ Nepali 4️⃣ Maithili
questions.e: The 71st Amendment added Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali. Maithili was added later by the 92nd Amendment.

questions.q: As per Article 368 of the Constitution of India, the Parliament may amend any provision of the Constitution by way of: 1️⃣ Addition 2️⃣ Variation 3️⃣ Repeal
questions.e: Article 368 explicitly states that Parliament can amend "by way of addition, variation or repeal" any provision of the Constitution.
